label: Stress level effect
summary: Something about the effect of the character's stress level; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it gives the effects tied to the stress level. The game's player stress tooltip uses a function of the same name, which hints at the same meaning, but vanilla never names it on a character.

label: Stress progress text
summary: Probably a text about how far the character's stress has progressed; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and the player stress tooltip, which uses a function of the same name next to the stress level and its effects. Vanilla never names it on a character.

label: Take unowned legend
summary: A command that makes the character take over a legend that has no owner.
details: Vanilla's legend chronicle window runs it on the player with the legend shown in that window. It is wrapped in the command helpers: one posts it on click, one checks if it can be done, one shows its description as the tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a legend (vanilla passes the window's legend)

label: Lessee approves of liege
summary: Whether the theocratic lessee approves of their liege.
details: The council window uses it together with 'has approval status' to pick a frame (an icon picture): the first frame when there is a status and it is approving, the second otherwise. Going by its name, it is about the character as a theocratic lessee and that lessee's liege; the game documents nothing more.

label: Lessee has approval status
summary: Whether the theocratic lessee has an approval status towards their liege.
details: The council window combines it with 'lessee approves of liege' to pick which frame of an icon to show. Going by its name, it is about the character as a theocratic lessee; the game documents nothing more.

label: Pin or unpin character
summary: Toggles whether the character is pinned, going by its name.
details: Vanilla runs it from click handlers in the outliner (where one button is an unpin button), the interaction menu and shared buttons. It is an action, not a value. That pinned characters appear in the outliner is an inference from the first use.

label: Uses obedience
summary: Whether the character is in a setup where obedience applies.
details: Vanilla checks it in the shared lists together with 'has an overlord' and 'is obedient to' the overlord, to show or hide parts of a list. Going by those uses, it says whether obedience matters for this character.

label: Uses treasury vassal development
summary: A yes or no about vassal development paid from a treasury; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it anywhere.

label: Was player
summary: Whether the character is or was played by a player.
details: It also holds for a character a player played earlier. Vanilla does not use it in the places searched.

label: Zoom camera to character
summary: Moves the camera to the character, going by its name.
details: Vanilla runs it from click handlers in the HUD. Its return type is void, so it is an action with no result. Which camera it moves is an inference from the name.

label: Filter preset itself
summary: The character filter preset itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other types to hand the object on, for example as an argument.

label: Preset description
summary: The description text of the character filter preset.
details: Going by its name and its text return. Vanilla uses the same name on other types (buildings, government types, activities) for their descriptions, but not on this type.

label: Preset name
summary: The name of the character filter preset.
details: Vanilla uses it in the character list's filter button text: 'Active filters:' followed by this name.

label: Filter preset itself
summary: The character filter preset itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function, such as 'Character.Self'.

label: Finder window itself
summary: The character finder window itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other windows to hand on the window object.

label: Close finder window
summary: Closes the character finder window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the window's close button.

label: Finder character list
summary: The list of characters the character finder window shows.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of the window's list part, so the part can show the characters.

label: Finder window itself
summary: The character finder window itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function.

label: Focus window itself
summary: The character focus window itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other windows to hand on the window object.

label: Can change focus
summary: Whether the player can change the character's focus right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable or disable the window's primary button (labelled CHOOSE_FOCUS), whose tooltip is the can-change description and whose click is the focus change.

label: Close focus window
summary: Closes the character focus window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the window's close button.

label: Why focus can't change
summary: The text that says whether, and why, the focus can or cannot be changed.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the button that confirms the focus change.

label: Focus window character
summary: The character the focus window is about.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of the whole window, so the parts inside read from this character.

label: Disposition frame
summary: The picture frame number for one of the window's disposition icons.
details: Vanilla calls it with 0, 1 and 2 to choose which frame of an icon to show. Going by its name and these uses, the number picks one of the three entries.

label: Focus by position
summary: The focus at a given position among the choices of the focus window.
details: Vanilla calls it with 0, 1 and 2 and gives each result as the data context of one of the window's three focus parts.

label: Focus description
summary: The description text of a focus, taken from the game's focus data.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the focus window.

label: Focus icon tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for a focus icon.
details: Going by its name and its text return. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which focus the tooltip is for (meaning not shown by the game).

label: Selected focus description
summary: The description text of the focus currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the focus window.

label: Selected focus effects
summary: The text listing what the currently selected focus does.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the focus window.

label: Selected focus modifiers
summary: The text listing the modifiers of the currently selected focus.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the focus window.

label: Selected focus name
summary: The name of the focus currently selected in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text, and hides the name part when it is empty (no focus selected).

label: Focus warning text
summary: A warning text shown in the focus window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window. The game does not say what the warning is about.

label: Focus window title
summary: The title text of the character focus window.

label: Is character focus
summary: Whether the window is showing the focus kind with the given number.
details: Vanilla calls it with 0, 1 and 2 to show or hide a part of the window. Going by those uses, the number picks one of the window's kinds of focus; the game does not say which is which.

label: Is focus available
summary: Whether the given focus can be chosen; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Which focus (meaning not shown by the game).

label: Is selected focus
summary: Whether the focus at the given position is the one currently selected.
details: Vanilla calls it with 0, 1 and 2 to show the matching focus button as pressed.

label: Confirm focus change
summary: Changes the character's focus to the one selected in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the window's primary button (CHOOSE_FOCUS), which is only enabled when the focus can be changed.

label: Select focus
summary: Selects the focus at the given position in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it with 0, 1 and 2 from the clicks of the three focus buttons. It only selects; the change is made by the confirm button.

label: Focus window itself
summary: The character focus window itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function.

label: Interaction itself
summary: The character interaction itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other types to hand on the object.

label: Alert icon
summary: The alert icon of the interaction; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Interaction icon
summary: The icon of the interaction, for a given character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a picture in the title window, giving a character as the argument. Going by its name, the icon can depend on that character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the icon is for.

label: Scheme type
summary: The scheme type of the interaction, going by its name.
details: Its return type is a scheme type. The game documents nothing more; vanilla uses a function of the same name on schemes, not on interactions.

label: Has alert icon
summary: Whether the interaction has an alert icon; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Interaction itself
summary: The character interaction itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function.

label: Show effects in notification
summary: Whether the notification of the interaction lists its effects.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's notification windows, which use it to show or hide the effects part. Vanilla names it there through the notification window, not on this type directly.

label: Shows military strength
summary: Whether the interaction's confirmation shows military strength.
details: Going by vanilla's confirmation window, which uses it to show a military strength part or hide it. Vanilla names it there through the window's interaction, not on this type directly.

label: Uses artifact target
summary: Whether the interaction needs an artifact as its target.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's confirmation window, which shows the artifact picking part when it is true. Vanilla names it there on the window, not on this type.

label: Uses title target
summary: Whether the interaction needs a title as its target.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's confirmation window, which shows the title part when it is true (together with other conditions). Vanilla names it there on the window, not on this type.

label: Category itself
summary: The interaction category itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other types to hand on the object.

label: Category background
summary: The background picture of the interaction category; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses the same name on other types (bookmarks, activities) as a texture.

label: Category color
summary: The color of the interaction category, as a four-part vector.
details: Going by the type name, the four numbers are probably red, green, blue and alpha. Vanilla uses the same name on the category item of the interaction templates as the color of a part.

label: Category description
summary: The description text of the interaction category.
details: Vanilla uses it in the 'Show more ...' tooltip text of the interaction window.

label: Category icon
summary: The icon of the interaction category.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses the same name on other types as a texture, but not on this type.

label: Category name
summary: The name text of the interaction category.
details: Going by its name and its text return; the game does not say what the argument is. Vanilla uses the same name on other types, not on this one.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: An extra value the name is built with (not shown by the game).

label: Has background
summary: Whether the interaction category has a background picture; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the interaction category has an icon; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses the same name on other types (concept tooltips, laws) to show an icon only if there is one.

label: Category itself
summary: The interaction category itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function.

label: Scheme info
summary: The scheme information shown in the interaction confirmation window.
details: Vanilla reads the odds prediction breakdown from it in the interaction templates.

label: Confirmation window itself
summary: The interaction confirmation window itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other windows to hand on the window object.

label: Can change actor
summary: Whether the player can change who the acting character is in the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part in the interaction templates. The meaning is taken from the name.

label: Can change recipient
summary: Whether the player can change who receives the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part in the interaction templates. The meaning is taken from the name.

label: Can change title
summary: Whether the player can change the title chosen for the interaction; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Can clear
summary: Whether the choices made in the window can be cleared.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable or disable a part in the interaction templates; going by the name, the clear button.

label: Can revert actor
summary: Whether the acting character can be set back to the original one.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part in the interaction templates. The meaning is taken from the name.

label: Can revert recipient
summary: Whether the recipient can be set back to the original one.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part in the interaction templates. The meaning is taken from the name.

label: Can select anybody
summary: Whether any character can be picked in the window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Can send
summary: Whether the interaction can be sent now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable or disable the send button of the confirmation window. 'Get can send description' gives the matching tooltip text.

label: Close confirmation window
summary: Closes the interaction confirmation window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the window's close button.

label: Acceptance breakdown
summary: A text for a listed character's acceptance, going by its name a breakdown of the acceptance value.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of a character in the list, giving that list entry as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character list item (vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self)

label: Acceptance value
summary: The acceptance value of a listed character, a number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 0 to show one part when it is above 0 and another when it is 0 or less. It returns a fixed-point number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character list item (vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self)

label: Actor
summary: The character who carries out the interaction.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more. Vanilla names it only through other types in the lines given.

label: Actor secondary label
summary: A second label text for the acting character.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the interaction templates.

label: Answer text
summary: The answer text of the window; going by its name, the recipient's expected answer.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the interaction templates.

label: Answer progress
summary: How likely the recipient is to accept, as a fraction shown as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in the acceptance chance text and also gives it as a value to a part.

label: Answer reason
summary: A text for the answer's reason; going by its name, why the recipient answers as expected.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the interaction templates.

label: Answer score
summary: The acceptance score of the interaction, a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign in the acceptance score text and uses it in conditions of the interaction templates, together with the checks for an AI recipient.

label: Army composition
summary: The army composition of a listed character, going by its name.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a part in the interaction templates, with the list entry as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character list item (vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self)

label: Artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts that can be picked in the interaction window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of an artifact list in the interaction templates.

label: Can send description
summary: The text that tells whether and why the interaction can or cannot be sent.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the send button.

label: Candidate score
summary: The candidate score of a listed character.
details: Vanilla shows it as a rounded number in the list and in a tooltip heading that names the candidate score concept.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character list item (vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self)

label: Candidate score breakdown
summary: Going by its name, the breakdown of a listed character's candidate score.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a tooltip part, with the list entry as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character list item (vanilla passes CharacterListItem.Self)

label: Character list
summary: The list of characters that can be picked in the interaction window.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of the window's list.

label: Cost text
summary: The text that says what the interaction costs.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text, for example after 'Cost:' in the marriage interaction.

label: Cost tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the cost of the interaction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the confirmation and council task windows.

label: Debug info
summary: A debug text about the interaction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the confirmation window and the templates. The game does not say what the text holds.

label: Effects description
summary: Going by its name, the description of what the interaction does.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a text part in several interaction windows (blackmail, call ally and others).

label: Governor efficiency
summary: The governor efficiency of a character, as a number; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and the sort mode 'governor_efficiency' used with 'is sorted by'. Vanilla does not call it directly.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character (meaning not shown by the game).

label: Interaction
summary: The character interaction the window is about.
details: Vanilla reads from it, for example the interaction's icon and whether it shows military strength.

label: Interaction description
summary: The description text of the interaction; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its text return. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Interaction tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the interaction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the confirmation window.

label: Men-at-arms
summary: The list of regiments that can be picked in the interaction window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the interaction templates; the setter takes a regiment. Going by the name, 'Maa' is men-at-arms.

label: On-decline summary
summary: The text that sums up what happens if the interaction is declined.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text; it first checks 'has on-decline summary'.

label: Option by flag
summary: One option of the interaction, found by its flag; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Options
summary: The list of options of the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the options list in the confirmation window and the templates.

label: Options heading
summary: The heading text above the options list.
details: Vanilla shows the heading only when it is not empty.

label: Prompt
summary: The prompt text of the window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the interaction templates. The game does not say what the prompt holds.

label: Puppet or actor
summary: A character, going by its name the puppet or else the acting character.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of character parts in many interaction windows. What a puppet is here the game does not say.

label: Recipient
summary: The character who receives the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of character parts and reads from it, for example the name in 'Take ... as my Concubine'.

label: Recipient secondary label
summary: A second label text for the recipient.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the interaction templates.

label: Scheme info
summary: The scheme information of the interaction.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a part in the confirmation window.

label: Secondary actor
summary: A second character, going by its name on the acting side.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a character part, for example in the claimant faction interaction.

label: Secondary recipient
summary: A second character, going by its name on the receiving side.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a character part in the interaction templates.

label: Selected artifact
summary: The artifact currently picked in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as a data context and compares it with each artifact in the list to show which one is chosen.

label: Selected men-at-arms
summary: The men-at-arms regiment currently picked in the window.
details: Vanilla reads its name for a text in the confirmation window.

label: Selected title
summary: The title currently picked in the window.
details: Vanilla gives it as a data context and checks whether it is valid.

label: Send button text
summary: The text of the button that sends the interaction.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text on the send button, in some windows chosen between this and another text.

label: Window picture
summary: The picture the interaction window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in several interaction windows, such as marriage and the templates.

label: Titles
summary: The list of titles that can be picked in the interaction window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data model, and counts its entries for a text.

label: Top character item
summary: Going by its name, the topmost entry of the window's character list.
details: Vanilla gives it as the data context of a part; 'has top character item' says whether there is one.

label: Visible options count
summary: How many options are shown in the window, as a whole number; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Has cost
summary: Whether the interaction costs something.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the cost part only then.

label: Has exclusive options
summary: Whether the interaction has options of which only one can be chosen.
details: Vanilla checks it, with the incite holy war check, to decide what the confirmation window shows.

label: Has interaction description
summary: Whether the interaction has a description text; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Has on-decline summary
summary: Whether there is a text that sums up what happens on decline.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the on-decline text part only then.

label: Has options
summary: Whether the interaction has options to pick.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the options part only then.

label: Has picked characters
summary: Whether the characters needed for the interaction have been picked.
details: Vanilla combines it with checks for picking a title, artifact or incite holy war to decide which parts of the window show.

label: Has selected artifact
summary: Whether an artifact has been picked in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the chosen artifact, or the prompt to choose one when it is false.

label: Has selected men-at-arms
summary: Whether a men-at-arms regiment has been picked in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the chosen regiment, or the prompt to choose one when it is false.

label: Has selected title
summary: Whether a title has been picked in the window.
details: Vanilla checks it, with the incite holy war check and the picked characters, in a trigger of the confirmation window.

label: Has top character item
summary: Whether the character list has a top entry.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the part for that entry only then.

label: Actor is recipient
summary: Whether the acting character and the recipient are the same person.
details: Vanilla uses it to hide the scheme part when they are the same.

label: AI accepts negotiation
summary: Whether an AI recipient is willing to negotiate; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla combines it with 'is AI maybe' and 'recipient is not a player' to decide which parts of the templates show.

label: AI is undecided
summary: Whether the AI recipient's answer is open (a maybe) rather than a sure yes or no.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla checks it together with 'recipient is not a player' to choose which parts the templates show.

label: Is answer positive
summary: Whether the expected answer is yes.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show one part or another.

label: Is forced to accept
summary: Whether the recipient has to accept the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to switch between two parts of the templates.

label: Is picking secondary actor
summary: Whether the player is now choosing the secondary actor.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the picking part only then.

label: Is picking secondary recipient
summary: Whether the player is now choosing the secondary recipient.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the picking part only then.

label: Is sorted by
summary: Whether the character list is sorted by the given criterion.
details: Vanilla calls it with 'candidate_score', 'governor_efficiency' and 'obedience' to show or hide a part for each sort.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the sort criterion.

label: Change or revert actor
summary: Going by its name, starts choosing another acting character, or sets it back to the original one.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the interaction templates, next to the checks for whether changing or reverting is possible.

label: Change or revert recipient
summary: Going by its name, starts choosing another recipient, or sets it back to the original one.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the interaction templates, next to the checks for whether changing or reverting is possible.

label: Clear choices
summary: Clears the choices made in the window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the clear button, which is enabled by 'can clear'.

label: Reload
summary: Reloads the confirmation window; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses a function of the same name on another type (an event window part) as a click action.

label: Confirmation window itself
summary: The interaction confirmation window itself, to pass as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses '.Self' on other types to hand the object itself to another function.

label: Send interaction
summary: Sends the interaction, going by its name, and returns a yes or no.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the send button, which is enabled by 'can send'. What the yes or no means the game does not say.

label: Select artifact
summary: Picks the given artifact for the interaction.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click on an artifact in the list, passing that artifact.

label: Select men-at-arms
summary: Picks the given men-at-arms regiment for the interaction.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click on a regiment in the list, passing that regiment.

label: Should pick secondary actor
summary: Whether a secondary actor has to be picked; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Should pick secondary recipient
summary: Whether a secondary recipient has to be picked; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Should show answer
summary: Whether the window shows the recipient's expected answer.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the answer part; the blackmail window shows it only when the window is a blackmail and this is true.

label: Should show scheme
summary: Whether the window shows scheme information.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to switch parts of the confirmation window.

label: Should show secondary recipient
summary: Whether the window shows the secondary recipient.
details: Vanilla uses it to show that part of the interaction templates only then.

label: Show four characters
summary: Whether the window uses the layout with four characters.
details: Vanilla uses it to show that layout only then.

label: Show three characters
summary: Whether the window uses the layout with three characters.
details: Vanilla combines it with the incite holy war check and a title change check to pick that layout.

label: Show two characters
summary: Whether the window uses the layout with two characters; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name and its siblings for three and four characters. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Uses artifact target
summary: Whether the interaction needs an artifact as its target.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the artifact picking part only then.

label: Uses men-at-arms target
summary: Whether the interaction needs a men-at-arms regiment as its target.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the regiment picking part only then.

label: Uses title target
summary: Whether the interaction needs a title as its target.
details: Vanilla combines it with the incite holy war check and the picked characters to show the title part.

label: Menu window itself
summary: The character interaction menu window itself, passed on to other functions.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses the same name on other windows to hand on the window object.

label: More interactions visible
summary: Whether more interactions are visible in the menu.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the interaction menu window. The 'Visisble' typo is the game's own spelling and must be kept.
